messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated error rate 5xx on /v1/generate EU region starting 22:47 UTC. Affected variant: v8-experimental (omega-variant). Automated metric spike + OOM traces detected.

eve_oncall: seeing it, I’m paged. pulling logs now. can someone confirm impact to customer-facing keys?

dinesh: quick check - spikes originated ~22:46, ~30% of predictions hitting the variant, error types look like OOM + kv-cache misses. stacktrace snippet shows `cuda out of memory` on pod gpu-omega-23.

carla: FYI support is getting inbound tickets from two customers in EU region, classified P1/P2.

eve_oncall: plan: temporarily disable v8-experimental routing, fail traffic to stable-3, and lower per-key rates for heavy keys. will also start canary rollback to stable-3 for warmup. opinions? :point_up:

dinesh: +1. recommend immediate `disable-variant` via control plane then apply emergency quotas for heavy keys. keep streaming enabled for others.

deploy-bot: Deploy request received: `action: disable_variant`, variant: `v8-experimental`, initiated_by: `eve_oncall`, trace_id: abcd-2248.

carla: if we disable cold we might spike latency on stable-3 if it’s not warmed. can we pre-warm some instances?

eve_oncall: good call. dinesh, can you trigger warmup and reduce concurrency limits on v8 before disable?

dinesh: doing `prefill_kv_cache` and a small warmup rollout to stable-3. commands:

```
# warmup stable-3 pool
redwoodctl pool scale --model stable-3 --region eu --replicas 6
redwoodctl warmup --model stable-3 --variant stable-3 --duration 120
```

then

```
# apply emergency quotas (per-key) and disable experimental variant
redwoodctl quota apply --scope keys-heavy --limit 10rps --duration 30m
redwoodctl variant disable --model my-model --variant v8-experimental --reason "OOM spike 22:46 UTC"
```

carla: sounds good. Support: please message affected customers with estimated mitigation window ~15-30m.

support-lead: sending outbound now. template: "We're investigating elevated errors in EU; routing to a stable variant; short degradation expected. We will update in 30 minutes."

deploy-bot: Variant `v8-experimental` disable started (job id: job-7788). Step 1/3: mark variant draining.

eve_oncall: monitoring error rate + latency, watching for drop in 5xx once drain completes. set alert to notify if stable-3 latency > 800ms.

dinesh: drain completed, variant has been disabled by job-7788. applying quota change.

deploy-bot: Variant `v8-experimental` disabled successfully. job-7788 complete.

carla: 5xx down from 18% -> 2% in 4m. client error reports reduced.

eve_oncall: good. keep an eye on cost — warmup increased throughput but temporary. can we set a short-lived throttle on anonymous keys to avoid thundering herd?

dinesh: applied `keys-anon` throttle: 5rps for 45m.

support-lead: updated customers: two P1s acknowledged, offered 1:1 mitigation assistance. no escalations yet.

ben: incoming handoff in 20m. anything I should watch for?

eve_oncall: summary for handoff -> root cause likely OOM on v8-experimental under EU load pattern (more long-context sessions). mitigation: disabled v8-experimental, warmed & routed to stable-3, emergency per-key quotas and anon throttle applied. customer comms sent. follow-ups: review v8 memory usage profile, consider quantization/kv-cache tuning, schedule postmortem.

dinesh: collecting heap profiles and KV hit-rate traces, will upload to /incidents/2248600000/artifacts.

eve_oncall: handing off to ben for the overnight watch. ben, take over at 23:10 UTC. note: if stable-3 latency > 900ms or 5xx >5% re-engage paging.

ben: ack takeover. I’ll monitor dashboards and coordinate with eng-runtime if anything regresses.

IncidentBot: Pager handoff recorded: from `eve_oncall` to `ben` at 23:10 UTC.

carla: adding task to backlog: "v8-experimental: memory regression triage & kernel selection audit". tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml.

support-lead: final note: all affected customers notified; triage is in progress; we will post incident update after postmortem scheduled. :white_check_mark:
